title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government confirms it will set clear, public standards for AI that include transparency, accountability, and risk‑assessment rules. It also promises to work with industry, academia, and overseas partners to update laws, support ethical AI research, and make sure AI systems serve society safely.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will monitor and regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector to keep assessments fair and reliable. The policy was released after requests from the Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade secretaries to protect the integrity of student exams and qualifications.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report evaluates how copyrighted works are used to train AI systems, examining the legal, ethical, and economic implications of that practice. It offers recommendations for balancing creators’ rights with the needs of AI development to guide policymakers, industry, and researchers.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has released a formal response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on AI, acknowledging the urgent need for clear oversight and safeguards around emerging technologies. It outlines plans to strengthen AI governance, support innovation, and promote responsible development while addressing risks and maintaining the country’s competitive edge.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the duties, scope, and objectives of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence relates to public standards. It also includes frequently asked questions to explain the committee’s role and what the review aims to accomplish.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee regarding the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission likely contains the organisation’s recommendations and concerns about how AI should be regulated and overseen.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This document examines how artificial intelligence will influence the rules and standards for medical products, focusing on ensuring safety, efficacy, and compliance. It outlines how the AI White Paper's principles can be integrated into regulatory frameworks to promote responsible innovation and protect public health.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: This Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy explains how the organisation will use AI to become the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential defence body in the world for its size. It focuses on deploying AI technologies to improve operations, decision‑making, and overall technological leadership in defence.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan shows how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to use artificial intelligence to improve services and efficiency. It also explains how the government will address and manage the risks and challenges that AI could bring to transport.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report examines how copyright‑protected works are being used to train and develop AI systems, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It reviews current practices, identifies challenges, and offers recommendations to better align AI development with copyright law and data‑use regulations.
